finding: CI-8 MED Caddy/IPv6 via docker userland proxy → all IPv6 share rate-limit bucket & login lockout.

commits.subject: Defer the public-edge topology change (CI-8) to a planned rollout
commits.body:
Reverts a2b795c3 from this integration; the commit stays ready to apply.
It fixes a real problem — behind Docker's userland proxy every IPv6 client
reaches Caddy from one bridge address and shares one login-lockout and
request budget — but only by moving Caddy to host networking, publishing
the app on host loopback and re-pinning the Compose network to
172.30.0.0/24, with the gateway trusting forwarded addresses only from that
gateway. The app half is inert without the topology half, and the next
deploy would have to recreate the production network (and reserve the
subnet on the host) inside an automatic update with no maintenance window.
That is the owner's rollout to schedule, not a side effect of merging a
large review branch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Preserve client addresses through the public edge

declaring `labels:` as a YAML block list (`- a` items) silently had no
labels, and `importance: high` was dropped to the default order. Read a
`- item` list under an empty key as a comma list, map low/medium/high
(and neighbours) onto the numeric scale pages already use, and treat an
unknown word or blank value as absent rather than 0 so a builtin's own
order still applies.
